clue.text: Electoral tie may hold up the motorist

explanation.surface: A dead-heat election result somehow brings traffic to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied vote is a crossing where the voters' crosses are level, and a railway barrier across a road stops drivers while trains pass.

clue.text: Mine host at the Town Hall ?

definitions.text: Mine host at the Town Hall ?

parts.words: Mine host at the Town Hall ?
parts.note: the landlord of the neighbourhood pub, the local, is in charge of it, while the town council sits at the Town Hall

explanation.surface: A publican who has wandered into the civic offices.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British neighbourhood pub, and its landlord ('mine host') is the authority there; the phrase also names a town council.
explanation.definitionFit: The council running a town is its civic government, housed in the Town Hall, and a pub landlord rules the bar of the local.

clue.text: Half a dozen, and only one item on the menu

definitions.text: only one item on the menu

parts.note: half a dozen is six, written VI in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: Six things ordered, and the menu offers just a single dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an old word for an article of food, a single dish.

clue.text: Unusual way Le Bulletin announces a shipwreck

indicators.note: set out in an unusual way, the letters of the French paper's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French newspaper breaks the news of a ship lost at sea in an odd fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual way' rearranges LE BULLETIN. The bell at Lloyd's of London, salvaged from HMS Lutine, was traditionally rung when news of a lost ship came in.
explanation.definitionFit: The salvaged ship's bell at Lloyd's of London was struck to signal that a vessel had been lost.

clue.text: Old parliament went ahead in disorder

parts.note: the Rump Parliament was the remnant of the Long Parliament after Pride's Purge in 1648
to lead is to go ahead, so went ahead is led

explanation.surface: A seventeenth-century parliament pressed on amid chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crumpled and untidy is in disarray.

clue.text: Runs at Wimbledon

parts.note: cricket runs scored one at a time, and the one-against-one tennis events played at Wimbledon

explanation.surface: Someone jogging around the tennis club in south-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon hosts the leading tennis championships; in cricket a run taken one at a time has the same name as its one-player-a-side events.
explanation.definitionFit: One-run scores in cricket and one-on-one tennis matches share this name.

clue.text: How certain worms progress, or how far ?

explanation.surface: A naturalist asking how fast, and how far, worms travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Looper caterpillars move along by edging forward, and a small span is a twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: Nice revolutionary wear for Women's Lib ?

explanation.surface: Clothing from a Riviera radical recommended to feminist campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective: the Italian patriot was born there. His followers' red shirts inspired a loose women's blouse named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian unification leader came from Nice, and a Victorian ladies' blouse copied his redshirts' style.

clue.text: They take turns to select a lucky number

definitions.text: They take turns to select a lucky number

parts.words: They take turns to select a lucky number
parts.note: devices that spin round and stop with a ball resting on one numbered pocket, choosing a winner at a casino

explanation.surface: People sharing out the job of picking a prize number.
explanation.definitionFit: Casino spinning discs come to rest with the ball on a single numbered slot.

clue.text: "Copper for the —— cunning at his trade" (Kipling)

definitions.text: "Copper for the —— cunning at his trade" (Kipling)

parts.words: "Copper for the —— cunning at his trade" (Kipling)
parts.note: the missing word completes a line of Kipling's poem Cold Iron, after gold for the mistress and silver for the maid

explanation.surface: A line of Kipling with a word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem Cold Iron runs 'Gold is for the mistress, silver for the maid, Copper for the ___ cunning at his trade'; the blank is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled worker cunning at his trade is the artisan of Kipling's line.

clue.text: In the hold of Adriatic argosies

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Something stowed below decks on merchant ships of the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of 'adriatiC ARGOsies'; argosies are large merchant ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried in a ship's hold are its freight.

clue.text: Loaded so start looking to the port

indicators.note: the start of the word looking gives its opening letter

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A heavily laden ship looks towards the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the port' seems a direction (port meaning left); here it is just the Yemeni port of Aden.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden is the old past participle of lade, meaning loaded with a burden.

clue.text: Compose the start of a song for children

indicators.note: only the opening part of the song's name is kept, its ending trimmed off

parts.note: a lullaby is a song sung to send children to sleep

explanation.surface: An instruction to write the opening bars of a nursery song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compose' looks like 'write', but here means 'calm', as one composes oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose someone is to soothe and quieten them.

clue.text: Prime sheep keeper

parts.note: Genesis says Adam's second son was a keeper of sheep, the first shepherd in the Bible

explanation.surface: An award for the best shepherd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like 'excellent'; it means first: Genesis 4:2 says Adam's son 'was a keeper of sheep', the first such keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the brother of Cain tended flocks, the earliest herdsman named in scripture.

clue.text: Spouter on a barrel ? Let's beat it !

parts.note: a kettle has a spout, so it is a spouter
a drum is a cylindrical barrel or container

explanation.surface: An orator on a soapbox invites the crowd to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. 'Beat it' reads as 'leave', but the answer is an instrument you beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A timpani is a percussion instrument, something one strikes with sticks.

clue.text: Devious bounder defrocked

indicators.note: devious means winding or roundabout, so the letters of the word bounder take a different path

explanation.surface: A scheming cad of a priest has been stripped of his office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defrocked' suggests a disgraced priest; here it is literal: with the robes taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be defrocked is literally to have the gown removed, leaving one undressed.

clue.text: Groovy work for groups aiming for the top twenty

definitions.text: Groovy work for groups aiming for the top twenty

parts.words: Groovy work for groups aiming for the top twenty
parts.note: pop bands chasing the charts cut tracks pressed into the grooves of a vinyl disc

explanation.surface: A trendy job for bands hoping to make the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' looks like sixties slang for 'cool' but means literally 'cut in grooves', like a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop groups make studio tracks pressed into grooved vinyl discs for release.

clue.text: Minister requires division, and the answer's a fish

annotationWithheld.why: Minister requires division, and the answer's a fish (7), STERLET: the fish is the definition, but no parse found accounts for 'Minister requires division' and 'the answer's' giving STERLET; the wordplay is unclear
annotationWithheld.clue: Minister requires division, and the answer's a fish

clue.text: He gives the candidate his oral examination

definitions.text: He gives the candidate his oral examination

parts.words: He gives the candidate his oral examination
parts.note: a political candidate at a public meeting is tested by shouted interruptions from the audience

explanation.surface: An examiner conducting a viva for a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candidate' and 'oral examination' suggest a university viva; the candidate is standing for election and the 'examination' is shouted questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person shouting challenges at a speaker puts the would-be member of parliament on the spot.

clue.text: Understand about Miss Doolittle's conversion

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning

indicators.note: a conversion changes the form of something, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady

explanation.surface: Grasping how the flower girl in Pygmalion was transformed into a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversion' asks you to rearrange a name the clue only hints at: Shaw's flower girl, whose transformation into a lady is the story of Pygmalion. The indicator works on her first name, not on the printed words.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to see it clearly in the mind.

clue.text: Stealthy nature of some burglars

parts.note: thieves who climb silently into upper windows are called cat burglars, after the animal's quiet movement

explanation.surface: A description of how certain housebreakers operate.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving silently and gracefully, like a feline, describes a cat burglar's manner.

clue.text: It can give you the wind up at sea

definitions.text: It can give you the wind up at sea

parts.words: It can give you the wind up at sea
parts.note: on a ship a rotating drum is wound round to haul in cable, raising the anchor

explanation.surface: Something that frightens sailors on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give you the wind up' is British slang for frighten; here it means wind up, as a cable is wound on a ship's drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's vertical revolving drum is turned to wind in anchor cable or hawsers.

clue.text: Uncommon, finding radium with rhenium

parts.note: Ra is the chemical symbol for radium
Re is the chemical symbol for rhenium

explanation.surface: Chemists discover two scarce elements together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce or seldom found is unusual.

clue.text: The Moon was the largest on Campden Hill

definitions.text: The Moon was the largest on Campden Hill

parts.words: The Moon was the largest on Campden Hill
parts.note: in Chesterton's The Napoleon of Notting Hill the street lights of Campden Hill are outshone by the moon, the biggest light of all

explanation.surface: A note on the moon's size seen from a London hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: Campden Hill is a district of Kensington in west London; G. K. Chesterton's The Napoleon of Notting Hill turns on its street lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon shining over the hill is the greatest of the lights that illuminate it.

clue.text: Ground an oblate spheroid

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson about the shape of the soil beneath us.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil is called ground, and our planet is a sphere flattened at the poles.

clue.text: That which is opposite the left hand bank of the river ?

parts.note: the opposite of the left hand is the right hand, abbreviated RH
one is a pronoun standing for that which, as in the right-hand one

explanation.surface: A question about what lies across from the left bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'left bank' points to Paris's Rive Gauche; the right-hand one is a French river flowing through Lyon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river of Switzerland and France.

clue.text: To perform in the Italian creates an image

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the Italian article

parts.note: il is Italian for the
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Acting in the Italian theatre makes a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a statue or likeness worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Extinct class of commuter

parts.note: British Railways abolished its lowest ticket class in 1956, leaving only first and second

explanation.surface: A naturalist classifies a vanished species of daily traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extinct' and 'class' sound biological; the class is a railway ticket grade that British trains no longer sell.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest ticket grade below second on British trains was dropped in 1956.

clue.text: Peer is not placed to put his oar in

indicators.note: placed means set in a new position, so the letters of the three words are laid out again

explanation.surface: A lord who is not in the right position to interfere.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to intervene or interrupt in a matter that is someone else's concern.

clue.text: Colourful figures of the cycling years

definitions.text: Colourful figures of the cycling years

parts.words: Colourful figures of the cycling years
parts.note: numbers marking a year's place in the nineteen-year lunar cycle, once printed in gilt in calendars, hence colourful

explanation.surface: Vivid characters from the early days of the bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling years' suggests bicycles; it refers to the 19-year Metonic cycle of the moon used in fixing Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Each year's position in the Metonic lunar cycle, used to date Easter, was traditionally shown in gold in calendars.
